text: When the wall had been rebuilt and I had set up the doors, the gatekeepers, the singers, and the Levites were appointed.
I put my brother Hanani, together with Hananiah the commander of the citadel, in charge of Jerusalem, for he was a trustworthy man who feared God more than most.

I said to them, "The gates of Jerusalem are not to be opened until the sun is hot, and while the gatekeepers are still on duty the doors are to be shut and barred. Appoint guards from among the residents of Jerusalem, each at his post, each in front of his own house."
The city was large and spacious, but the people in it were few, and no houses had been rebuilt.

Then my God put it into my heart to assemble the nobles, the officials, and the people to be registered by families. I found the genealogical record of those who had come up first, and I found written in it:
These are the people of the province who came up from the captivity of the exiles, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away, and who returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own town.
They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:
of Pahath-moab, through the line of Jeshua and Joab, 2,818;
The men of Bethlehem and Netophah, 188;
the men of Kiriath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, 743;
the men of Ramah and Geba, 621;
the men of Bethel and Ai, 123;
the men of the other Nebo, 52;
the descendants of the other Elam, 1,254;
The priests: the descendants of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, 973;
The Levites: the descendants of Jeshua, through Kadmiel, of the line of Hodevah, 74.
The singers: the descendants of Asaph, 148.
The gatekeepers: the descendants of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai, 138.
The temple servants: the descendants of Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth,
The descendants of Solomon's servants: the descendants of Sotai, Sophereth, Perida,
All the temple servants and the descendants of Solomon's servants numbered 392.
The following came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer, but they could not prove that their families and their descent were from Israel:
the descendants of Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda, 642.
And among the priests: the descendants of Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai — the one who had married a daughter of Barzillai the Gileadite and took his family name.

versions.text: And among the priests: the descendants of Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai, who had married a daughter of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.
versions.explanation: As it stands, "who had married" can be heard as referring to the descendants rather than to the ancestor, and "called by their name" is unclear when read aloud. The revision clarifies both without adding content.

text: These searched for their family records, but they could not be found, so they were excluded from the priesthood as unclean.

The governor ordered them not to eat any of the most holy food until a priest should arise to consult the Urim and Thummim.[^1]

[^1]: Urim and Thummim: sacred objects kept by the high priest and used to seek God's decision.

versions.text: The governor ordered them not to eat any of the most holy food until a priest should arise to consult the Urim and Thummim.
versions.explanation: "Urim and Thummim" is opaque to most hearers; a brief footnote aids comprehension without altering the reading text. (The Hebrew title Tirshatha is well rendered as "the governor.")

text: besides their male and female servants, of whom there were 7,337. They also had 245 male and female singers.

The governor gave to the treasury 1,000 gold darics, 50 bowls, and 530 priestly garments.[^1]

[^1]: The Hebrew title here is *Tirshatha*, a Persian term for a provincial governor. A daric was a Persian gold coin; a mina was a weight of silver.

versions.text: Some of the heads of families contributed to the work. The governor gave to the treasury 1,000 gold darics, 50 bowls, and 530 priestly garments.
versions.explanation: A brief footnote explaining the Persian title and the unfamiliar units (daric, mina) would help hearers who cannot pause to look them up; the terms recur in the following verses.

text: Others among the heads of families gave to the treasury for the work 20,000 gold darics and 2,200 minas of silver.

versions.text: Some of the heads of families gave to the treasury for the work 20,000 gold darics and 2,200 minas of silver.
versions.explanation: Verses 69 and 70 open with the identical English phrase, which blurs the distinction the Hebrew makes between מִקְצָת ("some of") in v. 69 and מֵרָאשֵׁי ("from the heads") here. Varying the opening helps a listener hear that a second, separate group of donors is being described.

text: And what the rest of the people gave was 20,000 gold darics, 2,000 minas of silver, and 67 priestly garments.

So the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the temple servants, and all Israel settled in their towns. When the seventh month came, the Israelites were in their towns.
